newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CKD PRAHA SEES 1996 LOSS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CKD PRAHA SEES 1996 LOSS.

text.p: Czech engineering concern CKD Praha a.s. said on Wednesday it expected to post a 1996 consolidated loss of less than one billion crowns, after an 87 million net profit in 1995.
The firm's finance director, Jiri Simek, told Reuters the loss, which is lower than the originally expected 1.7 billion crown loss, was caused by write-offs of some non-performing assets.

"I expect that we will be able to eliminate (a part of) the accounting loss, so it should go under one billion crowns," Simek said adding much of the write-offs were from the firm's three billion crowns of receivables from Russia.
He added that the company expected to return to profitability this year, posting a net profit of 490 million crowns.

Simek CKD's preliminary operating profit last year was flat at 750 milion crowns, while sales rose to some 9.4 billion crowns from 8.7 billion in 1995. Simek said he expected revenues to rise to 11.2 billion this year.
